findings.evidence: “number the options, accept several numbers where a step says `multiSelect: true`, and wait for the answer” spells out a familiar conversational fallback. The expert constraint is that a headless run cannot substitute for owner consent.
findings.fix: Keep one portable rule here: use the host's question tool or ask the owner directly, preserving multi-select; without either channel, take the headless branch. Record the removal of the generic numbering mechanics.

findings.evidence: The valid 1,013-character description spends a full sentence on the wizard's internal sequence (“Detects installed CLIs and models, proposes … asks each role's order”) before reaching the trigger. Lead with what the owner wants to accomplish.
findings.fix: Use this skill to set up, refresh or check ai-kit's cross-AI reviewers and executors: add a second opinion, choose models to implement plans, or set each role's fallback order, even if the user never says “lanes”. Detect installed CLIs and models, propose catalog candidates for owner approval, and write `[lanes]` in `.aikit/config.toml` or the user `config.toml`. `--check-only` reports availability without writing config; `--local` and `--global` select a target but never authorize replacement. Also use when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers reports no lanes, to check stale opencode providers, or to report pending `review-spec.toml` migration. Not for running a review or execution with configured lanes, hand-editing one lane value, or changing `[runner]` or `opencode.jsonc`.

findings.evidence: “Build the JSON shape `python3 "$TOOLS_PY" render-toml` expects” opens a dense writer procedure that even headless and report-only runs load. The body has 5,126 whitespace-delimited words before tokenization, despite having clear reference gates elsewhere.
findings.fix: Keep the Step 3 decision gates and handoff to Step 4 inline. Put the writer JSON template, exact invocation, target recheck and stdout/stderr capture contract in `references/write-roster.md`; read it only after the owner has confirmed a roster or explicitly requested a clear.

findings.evidence: “When an entry was shown at step 4 instead of its own preview line” still allows the trusting call on a yes. In the documented same-key case, the owner may see the execute row's fields but not the resolved invocation; the post-write field check cannot tell them what would run.
findings.fix: Continue showing those fields for diagnosis, but stop with the project roster untrusted whenever a command-bearing entry lacks its own resolved preview. Offer trust only once the preview can show every affected role and key.

findings.evidence: The check-only eval has `"files": []` but asserts both the branch where a lane has no confirmed read-only invocation and the branch where every lane is confirmed read-only. A single unseeded run does not establish both, or even ensure the probe has a lane to inspect.
findings.fix: Split this into two cases with fixture rosters and stubbed profile or detection output. In one, decline the probe and assert no `probe-quota` call; in the other, accept it and assert the throwaway quota path, no persistent config or cache changes, and scratch cleanup.

findings.evidence: The suite has 12 positives and 10 negatives; “Which providers … are no longer listed?” substantially duplicates the stale-provider trigger at line 6. The set does not directly test the boundary between checking lane availability and explaining a past dispatch.
findings.fix: Use 10 distinct positives and 10 near-miss negatives. Consolidate overlapping setup and provider positives, and make one contrast explicit: check which configured lanes are available now (trigger) versus explain why a past run selected a fallback without changing the roster (do not trigger).

findings.evidence: The global raw-read branch uses `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/ai-kit/config.toml`, but `cfg_config_base` ignores a relative XDG_CONFIG_HOME. With a relative value, `--check-only --global` can list a different file from the one the quota preflight resolves.
findings.fix: Use the absolute user-config path rule in `references/config-file.md` → Layers for check-only too. Add an example with a relative XDG_CONFIG_HOME that confirms the raw read uses the home fallback.

findings.evidence: “`render-toml` rejects anything else and prints why” is not true for arbitrary scalar lane keys. An in-memory render with `servce_tier = "fast"` succeeded and preserved the misspelled key, so exit 0 does not prove the requested tier was stored.
findings.fix: State the writer's actual validation scope. Before `--out`, compare the draft keys and values with Lane entry fields and any explicitly allowed custom template fields; flag misspelled knobs rather than expecting the writer to catch them.

findings.evidence: “Skip this section unless a preferred runtime has no listing” appears in Step 1.5, but preferred runtimes are first chosen in Step 2.2. If the owner later picks listing-less Copilot, the consented pane-discovery branch has no explicit return path.
findings.fix: Invoke Optional sources from `wizard-flow.md` step 2, after the owner chooses runtimes and before the permitted catalog refresh. Keep the existing pane consent and pending-migration gates.

findings.evidence: “An added lane counts as the fallback only once it is kept through those steps and is not usage-limited itself” omits the pool check for an owner-named alternative. A second free model in the same pool can pass those checks without being a selectable fallback.
findings.fix: Before ending the fallback question, apply the complete rule in section d to any added lane, including one typed by the owner: same role, not usage-limited, and outside the original lane's pool. If it fails, ask again or record an explicit decision to proceed without a fallback.

findings.evidence: “Free models of <provider> appear to share one pool (reported by users, not confirmed by the vendor)” applies a version-sensitive quota claim to every provider without a source or date. The emitted `pool_key` establishes ai-kit's fallback policy, not the provider's actual quota accounting.
findings.fix: Always explain the behavior ai-kit controls: it will not use another lane with that pool key as the fallback. Give provider-specific quota evidence only when it has a source and date; preserve the attribution and its uncertainty when citing a user report.
